This file is an Incident Package manifest — the unit GDD §25.8 states the content-lock gate at — and it binds an anomaly, a map and a premise that are all first-party to this project. licensingRecordId is null because there is no third-party material in the package to record, and this note is what makes that null mean 'checked, and here is why' rather than 'nobody has looked at this one'. §25.7's ShareAlike questions do not engage. The gate status and §25.3's field table are in content/provenance.json.
_note:
THE SECOND INCIDENT ON THE NINTH FLOOR, and the one that spends the half of the building the first one does not touch. `ashlar-gallery-draught` is a journey: the whole floor is a corridor to the heating gallery, the answer is a fence made of heat, and every wall on the way is either a wall or a hole depending on which of the two buildings you are walking. This one never leaves one flat. GDD §15.2 — the building is the constant and the incident is the variable — and the variable here is that the map's argument gets used from the other end.

ASHLAR'S ARGUMENT IS THAT NINETEEN OF FIFTY-SEVEN WALLS ARE REAL AND THIRTY-EIGHT ARE NOT. The draught incident is about the thirty-eight being useless: they stop the squad and not the thing, so the operatives go the long way round the flats while it crosses them in a straight line. This incident is about the thirty-eight being USEFUL, and for a reason nobody has needed yet: `observedBy` casts its sightlines against `blockingRects()`, which is all fifty-seven. A stud-and-plasterboard partition breaks a line of sight exactly as completely as a concrete crosswall does. So on this floor a wall that stops nothing can hide you from something, and hiding from it is the entire containment.

The lodger is in the south room of Flat 5, hard against the one surviving partition in that flat — static 55, 3.2m of plasterboard with a 2.2m gap at its east end. That partition is the incident. Stand north of it and you are unseen and 1.9m away, which is inside a 2.2m reach: the wall is PRIVACY AND NOT PROTECTION, and there is nowhere else in this build where those two can be separated by eleven millimetres.

Nothing here is where the draught incident put anything. Different flat, different half of the loop, different anchor, and not one shared coordinate.
_variationNote:
GDD §14.4. This floor varies in the WALK, in the state of the two temporary circuits, in which half of the paper trail is missing and in the two men who will talk to you. It does not vary in where the lodger is, and that is measured rather than assumed.

⚠ NO ORIGINS. THE FLAT IS BOTH THE INCIDENT AND THE REASON. The containment is hiding from it behind static 55, so every origin would have to be hard against a partition with a screen — and two of the three things worth reading in that flat ARE the thing's own footprint. `frost-band` is the burnt band on the partition beside it; `glazed-ring` is the hard edge of its 2.2m ring, drawn on the floor at 1:1. Both are authored just outside the reach on purpose, at 2.40m and 2.56m, so that a squad reads them from the wrong side and pays for it in nerve rather than in a contact. Move the lodger and the marks stay where they are: the band it burnt would sit three metres from it and the ring it polished would be off-centre, which is the file disagreeing with itself, and one of the two would fall inside 2.2m and turn a reading into a grab.

Measured on the shipped geometry, on a 0.05m grid over the whole south room: of 3300 cells, 282 are standable at the operative radius, keep all three of `frost-band`, `glazed-ring` and `dropped-tiles` outside the 2.2m reach, sit behind static 55 from the Flat 5 doorway, and still have a screened standing point within reach north of the partition to seal from. Those 282 are one patch 0.90m by 1.25m, and the authored origin is inside it. Allow a 0.2m margin on the reach and it collapses to 0.40m by 0.55m. There is one place in Flat 5 for this thing to be. Moving it with its own marks wants an origin bound to a named source in src/sim/variation.js — the origin and the civilian positions are drawn independently, so content cannot do it.

ROUTES: the lift lobby is the only cross-link in the middle of the plan and either of its doors kills it, so a jammed lobby turns a lap into the full circuit — north corridor, west link, south corridor, east link — and that circuit is exactly the distance between the watchman on the east landing and the fitter's kit at the west end of the south corridor. The four gallery doors are not on the list: nothing in this incident happens below the store rooms, so jamming one would be a jam that costs nothing and reads as a bug.

⚠ THE GALLERY CIRCUIT IS ON THE FAULT LIST HERE, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE CALL FROM ashlar-gallery-draught. Down there the gallery is the containment and faulting it makes the authored pen unbuildable. Up here nothing happens in it, all four of its doors start open and a dead circuit leaves them open, so the seed that spends its fault on the gallery is simply the seed on which the landing circuit can still be brought up and the shortcut bought. The other seed faults the landing circuit: no lobby, and the corridors stay on their three emergency luminaires for the whole night. That costs composure rather than sight — `lightAt` feeds `stepStress` and nothing in perception.js reads a luminaire — and it is the same harder-never-impossible night the gallery incident already measured on this map.

TWO SOURCES GO PER SEED, ONE PER RULE AT MOST. What is never on the list: `frost-band` and `glazed-ring`, because they are the thing's own marks and a floor that does not show them is a floor that does not agree with itself; `dropped-tiles`, because the north room is where a squad learns that walking in is enough BEFORE they walk in; and `thermal-void` and `helmet-footage`, because both cost cargo and a squad that bought the instrument has to have something to point it at. What is left is the four that are a walk and nothing else — the surveyor's logger on the meter tails, the day book two flats back, the handover sheet in the crew's mess and the meter-cupboard note at the far corner of the loop. `charger-note` is safe to lose because `pull-charge`'s second path is earned rather than found: `battery-drain` comes off the squad's own telemetry and cannot be taken off the floor.

The mate moves and the watchman does not. The mate is standing in the corridor either where he stopped, outside the Flat 5 door, or at the far end of it where he has backed off to; both are in the north corridor his label names and both are clear of the lobby door and of every other source by more than the 2.8m reach probe. The east landing is where the squad comes up and it already carries the cargo cache and the extraction point, so there is no second place on it to put a man. Both of them can be not keen, which is a longer conversation for the same sentence.
_spawnNote: The south room of Flat 5, 1.0m south of the partition's face and 1.2m west of its open east end. Checked standable against blockingRects() at the player radius, and checked against every fixture on the floor: the nearest door centre is the lift lobby's south door at 6.7m and the nearest breaker is the landing circuit at 9.9m, so the seal never competes with a fixture verb. The east end of the partition is deliberately close — 1.2m — because a squad that walks round it instead of standing behind it gets seen, and the difference between those two routes is one and a half metres.

briefing.headline: Two contractors withdrawn, condemned block, ninth floor
briefing.report: Ashlar House was decanted eleven months ago and is due for demolition. A strip-out contractor finished five of the six flats on the ninth and pulled his crew off the sixth after the third visit. One man came off with a cold burn and a broken wrist; the other walked out and will not go back up. The watchman has kept doing his rounds and says he has never had any trouble.

known.text: The site watchman is on the east landing and will give a statement.
Both circuits are on the contractor's temporaries and both are dead. Nothing on this floor is locked.
The injured man's kit is still on the ninth. His helmet camera is with it.
The second man puts it in Flat 5 and says it is against the middle wall.

_placementNote:
⚠ NEAREST-WINS, AND THIS FLOOR HAS BROKEN ON IT BEFORE. `contextAction` sorts candidates by distance, and `sourceInReach` probes reach + 0.6 = 2.8m. So a source inside 2.8m of another source can answer for it, and a source inside about 5m of a door centre or a breaker can beat the fixture from the spot an operative stands on to work it — which on the cold store took a whole containment out. Every source below was checked, by measurement rather than by eye, for four things: standable at the player radius; more than 2.8m from every other source; far enough from every door centre, breaker, the cargo cache and the extraction point that the fixture still wins from in front of it; and possessing at least one standable point at which it is the nearest interactable on the floor.

TWO OF THEM ARE DELIBERATELY INSIDE THE FLAT AND NEITHER IS INSIDE THE REACH. `frost-band` sits at the west end of the partition, 2.4m from the lodger, and `glazed-ring` sits at the east end of the south room, 2.6m from it. Both are outside 2.2m and both are read from the wrong side of the thing, so a squad that walks straight at either of them arms it on the way. That is the intended cost and it is authored rather than accidental: the flat has three things worth reading in it and the price of all three is the same.

The trail otherwise reads in the order a squad walks it — the watchman on the landing where they arrive, the day book and the housing file in the flats they pass, the mate and the imager position in the north corridor outside the door, the meter cupboard note out at the far corner of the loop in the west stair, the fitter's kit at the west end of the south corridor, and the ambulance sheet in the drying room the crew were using as a mess. `battery-drain` has no entry here on purpose; it is logged from the squad's own telemetry by game.js and cannot be walked to.

MEASURED, on the shipped geometry: thirteen sources, the tightest pair 3.00m apart against a 2.8m probe, and the closest any of them comes to a door centre, a breaker, the cache or the extraction point is 3.41m. Every one is standable at the player radius and every one has a standable ring position from which it is the nearest interactable on the floor.
